newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip in line with Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds dip in line with Treasuries.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities traded lower in line with Treasuries on Monday, slipping as much as 9/32 in discount coupons by late afternoon.

Pass-through securities performed on par with their Treasury counterparts after the Commerce Department said single-home sales rose 4.7 percent in August to an annual rate of 832,000 units, the highest rate in more than a decade.
Not suprisingly, Ginnie Mae pass-throughs outperformed other agency paper much of the day, traders said.

GNMAs may look better because they are more liquid than other agency issues, said a West Coast regional trader, adding that "on a quiet day like today, if somebody is doing anything at all, its impact is magnified."
By late afternoon, Ginnie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent coupons were off 6/32 at 100-30/32, yielding 120 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note.
Comparable Fannie Mae 30-year 8.0 percent pass-throughs were down 7/32 to 100-27/32, and Freddie Mac 30-years also slipped 7/32 to 101.
The 10-year note was off 8/32 to yield 6.71 in late trading.
